title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（大澤直樹研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Osawa Naoki)
teachers:
OSAWA Naoki
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal:
The aim of this course is to develop students' research and development skills in electrical and electronic engineering through research projects on plasma science and high-voltage engineering.
By the end of the course, students will be able to: 1.identify important research problems, 2.design effective problem-solving plans,3.carry out a research project,4.write a project report, and 5.deliver an oral presentation on their research findings.
advice:
[Projects]
(1) fundamental research on non-thermal plasmas and dielectric breakdown phenomena
Elucidation of mechanism on atmospheric pressure air diffuse dielectric barrier discharge generation, dielectric breakdown phenomena of solid/gas composite insulation, etc.
(2) applications of non-thermal plasmas
Ozone generation by non-thermal plasmas, air and water treatment, etc.

[Advice for learning]
Close communication with your team members or professor greatly enhances the progress of your research project.
books:
Textbooks: none
Reference books: [1] A. Fridman, "Plasma Chemistry", Cambridge University Press (2008), [2] J. Meichsner, M. Schmidt, R. Schneider, H.-E. Wagner, "Nonthermal Plasma Chemistry and Physics", Chapman and Hall/CRC (2012)
Reserved books: none
requiredKnowledge: Fundamental knowledge of electric circuits, electromagnetism, transient phenomena in electrical circuits, high-voltage and pulsed-power engineering, and machine tools (drilling, lathe, milling, etc.) is required. High voltages and high currents are extremely dangerous. To avoid the risk of electric shock, students must follow all safety regulations and instructions.

activityGoals.body: To be able to identify and clearly explain an important research problem.
To be able to design an effective plan for solving the problem.
To be able to carry out a research project.
To be able to communicate effectively with team members and/or the professor.
To be able to write a project report.
To be able to deliver a presentation at the DP-III final public defense.

achievementLevels.ideal: Students can:1.identify and explain an important problem from various viewpoints, 2.design a problem-solving plan from multiple perspectives, 3.carry out a research project, 4.communicate effectively with team members and/or the professor, 5.write a project report and an abstract for a domestic conference, and 6.deliver an oral presentation at the DP-III final public defense and at a domestic academic conference.
achievementLevels.standard: Students can: 1.identify and explain an important research problem, 2.design a plan for problem-solving, 3.carry out a research project, 4.communicate effectively with team members and/or the professor, 5.write a project report, and 6.deliver an oral presentation at the DP-III final public defense.

Ozone generation by non-thermal plasmas, air and water treatment, etc.
